new_findings.source: MathUtils.calculateLinearInterest: uint256 result = rate * (block.timestamp - uint256(lastUpdateTimestamp)); (checked 0.8 subtraction, then multiplication)
new_findings.issue: The bytecode checks block.timestamp - lastUpdateTimestamp for underflow unconditionally, before the multiplication's overflow test. The text puts that SafeMath.sub inside the right operand of 'rate and ...', so with currentLiquidityRate == 0 and lastUpdateTimestamp > block.timestamp the text returns the liquidity index where the bytecode reverts with Panic(17).
new_findings.rule: Never move an operation that can revert into the right operand of a short-circuit and/or whose left operand can skip it. A checked operation the bytecode evaluates on every path is printed as its own check (if b > a: revert) before the guarded test, as getReserveNormalizedVariableDebt does (line 1119).
